but has self bid farewell and said: I will again come to you (PL), if wills (it) Hashem, and has self sail away from Ephesus.
and coming to Caesarea, did he disembark and did offer up peace (visited) the kehile, and is down to Antioch.
and after the as he had (there) spent time a certain time, did he go away, and has passed through in turn the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all disciples.
and a certain Jew, with the name Apollos, born in Alexandria, an eloquent man, powerful in the scriptures (the Holy), is come to Ephesus.
the this one was taught in the way of Hashem; and being zealous in Spirit, did he speak and teach accurately what concerning Yehoshua, although he did only know the mikveh (of repentance) of John;
and did begin to speak with boldness in synagogue. when however Priscilla and Aquila did him heard, did they him take to themselves, and him more precisely clear made the way of Hashem.

wanting however to go to Achaia, did the brothers him give courage, and wrote to the disciples, that they should him receive; and when he is come there, did he much help the (ones), who did believe through the grace;
because with the entire power did he hold debates with the Jews, proving publicly from the scriptures (the Holy), that Yehoshua is the Moshiach.
and it is happened, when Apollos was in Corinth, did Paul, after to go through the interior parts of (Minor) Asia, come to Ephesus; and when he did (there) find some disciples,
did he to them say: (question) had you (PL) received were the Spirit the Holy, when you (PL) did become believers? did they say to him: we have even not heard, if there finds self a Spirit the Holy.
did he say: into what then did you (PL) self mikveh immersed? and they did say: in the mikveh of repentance of John.
did Paul say: John's mikveh was a mikveh of repentance, saying to the people, that they should believe in the one, who will come after him, that means in Yehoshua.
and on hearing this, did they themselves let immersed be in the mikveh in the name of the L-rd Yehoshua.
and when Paul did lay on them the hands, did the Spirit the Holy come on them; and they did speak with tongues and prophecies said.
and they all are was an about twelve men.
and he is gone in in synagogue, and did speak with boldness during of three months, holding debates and convincing about the kingdom of Hashem.

when however some did hard make their hearts and did not believe, speaking evil in relation to the way of (Hashem) before the crowd, did he go away from them, and did separate the disciples, and daily spoke in the house of learning yeshiva of a certain Tyrannus.
the these is went on two years long, so, that all inhabitants of (Minor) Asia, Jews and Greeks, did hear the word of the L-rd.
and Hashem has done extraordinary wonders through the hands of Paul;
such, that they used to take away from his body kerchiefs or aprons to the sick, and the diseases did them leave, and the evil spirits went out.

and some of the Jewish wanderers, masters of repute, did undertake to call upon the name of the L-rd Yehoshua for the (ones), who did have evil spirits, so to say: I adjure you (PL) by Yehoshua, whom Paul calls out!
and the (ones), who had this done are were seven sons of a certain Skeva, a Jew, one of the “great priests”.
and the evil spirit did answer and said to them: Yehoshua know I, Paul know I also; who however are you (PL)?
and the man, in whom was the evil spirit, did upon them a leap done, and overpowered both of them, and them (thus) defeated, that they did run away from that house naked and wounded.
and the these is known become to all Jews and Greeks, who did live in Ephesus; and a fear did fall on them all, and the L-rd Yeshua's name was raised up become.
and a many of the (ones), who did believe, did come and self confess was and report of their (earlier) deeds.

and a many of the (ones), who have self participated in magic/witchcraft, did bring together their (occult) books, and them burned before everyone in the eyes; and there (be) has counted up their worth, and found (that it did amount to) fifty thousand pieces of silver.
so powerful did grow the word of the L-rd and has itself strengthen.

and after the as the these things did happen, did Paul resolve in his spirit, that when he will have passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to travel to Jerusalem, and did say: after the when I will there be, must I also see Rome.
and dispatching to Macedonia two of the (ones), who did him aid, Timothy and Erastus, did he himself still remain a certain time in (Minor) Asia.
and around that time is happened not any small turmoil about the (Meshichistim) way of (Hashem).
because a certain man, with the name Demetrius, a silversmith, who used to make silver miniture shrines of Artemis, and give the craftsmen not any small income;
(he) did them gather and the (other) masters of trades of such items, and said: men, you (PL) know, that by the this work have we our prosperity.

and you (PL) see and hear, that not only in Ephesus, but almost in all (Minor) Asia did the this one Paul persuade and deserted a significant crowd of people, saying, that this are not any g-ds, which are made with hands;

and it is a danger, that not only our trade will become to mockery, but even the temple of the great g-ddess Artemis will for nought regarded become; and it could yet be, that there will taken away be the magnificence of her, whom all (Minor) Asia and the populated world worship.
and when they did this hear, did they become filled with wrath, and did shout, so to say: great is the Artemis of the Ephesians!
and the city is full become from the turmoil; and everyone together did storm to the theater, pulling along Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonian, Paul's companions on the journey.
when however Paul has wanted to go in among the people (mob), did the disciples him not permit.
and also some of the high officials (Asiarchs) of (Minor) Asia, being his friends, did send to him, and begged he shall himself not risk to come into theater into.
and they did shout, a part one thing, others something else, because the assembly was confused; and the most did not know, because of what they were themselves come together.
and from this crowd have they drag out Alexander, whom the Jews did push forward. and Alexander did make a sign with the hand, and wanted to make a defense speech before people (mob).
finding out (in anti-Semitism) themselves however, that he is a Jew, did all shout with one voice during of almost two hour; great is Artemis (the g-ddess) of the Ephesians!

and the city scribe, calming down the crowd people, did say: o men of Ephesus, (question) finds self then anyone among people, who knows not, that the city of the Ephesians is the temple keeper of the great Artemis and of her image, which did fall down from heaven?
therefore, since as there can the these things not dispute be, did you (PL) yourselves should keep calm, and nothing do in rashness.
because you (PL) have brought hither the these people, who are not any temple robbers, nor any blasphemers of our g-ddess.

therefore, if Demetrius and the craft workers with him have actually something a complaint against anyone, are (after all) being held publicly daily by courts, and there are here proconsuls; should they accuse one the other.
if however you (PL) seek something else, will it resolved become at the legal assembly.
because we are also in a danger, accused to become about an insurgency on account of this today action, because it is not any reason, with which we shall can account for the this riot.
and when he did this say, did he dismiss the assembly.
and after that as the turmoil has self calm down, did Paul send after the disciples and did speak words of comfort to them, has self bid farewell and is went out to go to Macedonia.
and passing through those provinces, and encouraging them (i. e. the there believers) with a many words, did he come to Greece.

and did (there) remain in the time of three months; and given that a plot is made become by the Judaeans against him, when he has plan had himself sail to Syria, did he decide himself to return over to Macedonia.

and up to (Minor) Asia was him accompanied Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea; and by the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius from Derbe, and Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus, from (Minor) Asia.
the these however had gone ahead, and did wait on us in Troas.
and after Pesach did we sail away with the ship from Philippi, and are in five days around come to them to Troas, where we did remain seven days.

and the first day of the week, when we did ourselves come together to break bread, did Paul preach to them, having in mind to the next morning to depart; and did extend was the sermon until half (midnight) night.
and there are was a many lamps in the room upstairs, where we are were gathered.

and on the window is sat a certain young man, with the name Eutychus, (who) is fall into in a deep sleep; and while Paul was still all prolonging with his preaching, did the sleep him overpowered, and he has fallen down from the third story, and they have him picked up a dead person.
Paul however did go down, and did fall on him, and embracing him, did he say: worry self not, because the soul his is (still) in him.
and did go up, did break the bread, and (himself) taste did, and then long with them spoke, till it is become dawn‎, and so did he depart.
and the young man have they brought leading a living, and they have self not a little comforted.
we however were going ahead to the ship, and have ourselves sailed away to Assos, so as there to collect Paul; because so has he ordered, because himself did he want to go on foot.
and when he has self with us met in Assos, did we him receive (onboard), and did come to Mitylene.
and further sailing away from there, did we the next day arrive opposite Chios; and the next day did we come to Samos; and the following day did we come to Miletus.
because Paul had decided to sail by Ephesus, so that he shall not need to lose any time in (Minor) Asia; because he has self hurried, as far possible for him, to be in Jerusalem for Shavuos.
and from Miletus did he send to Ephesus, and let call the elders of the kehile.
and when they did come to him, has he to they say:
serving the L-rd with all humility and with tears and trials, which did come on me by the intrigues of Judaeans;
how I did nothing hold back from you (PL) out of that, which is of benefit, that I shall it not have said to you (PL), and you (PL) taught, both publicly and from house to house,
witness saying to Jews and to Greeks about repentance to Hashem and faith in our L-rd Yehoshua the Moshiach.
and look, now, bound in the Spirit, go I to Jerusalem, not knowing, what it will me there meet,
except this, which the Spirit the Holy is testifying to me in every city, so to say, that there waiting on me chains and troubles.

but I consider, that my life is not worth the words, so precious is it for me, if I shall but can finish the life's journey mine, and the service, which I have received from the L-rd Yehoshua, witness to say of the Good News of Hashem's grace.
and look, now know I, that you (PL) will more never not see my face, you (PL) all, among whom I did go about, proclaiming the kingdom of Hashem.
therefore am I testify to you (PL) this today's day, that I am clean of the blood of all (people).
because I did me not hold back, you (PL) not to proclaim the entire counsel of the will of Hashem.
watch over then self and the entire flock, over which the Spirit the Holy did you (PL) appoint as overseers, so as to tend Hashem's kehile, which He did purchase with His own blood.
I know, that after my departure will come in among you (PL) evil wolves, who will not have any mercy on the flock;
and from you (PL) yourselves will arise men, who speak opposite things, drawing away the disciples after themselves.
on account of this shall you (PL) stand on the watch, remembering, that during of three years have I not ceased, by day and by night, to say reproof to every one of you (PL) with tears.
and now leave I you (PL) over on Hashem's counsel and to the word of his grace, which has the power you (PL) to build up and you (PL) to give the inheritance among all kedoishem.
silver, or gold, or clothing, have I from anyone not desired.
you (PL) alone know, that the these hands of mine have me served for my needs and for the needs of my companions.
all have I you (PL) shown, that laboring on such a way, must one help the weak, and remember the L-rd Yeshua's words, because he himself did say: it is better to give than to receive.
and after the when he had this said, did he bend his knees, and prayer did with them all.
and it is became among all a strong weeping, and they did fall Paul on the neck and did him kiss,
being painfully grieved, if mainly about the word, which he had said, that they would more not see his face—and did him accompany to the ship.

and it is happened, when we have ourselves separate and did went away from them, sailing away in a straight direction, course, did we come to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara;
and since we did find a ship, which was going to Phoenicia, did we board and sail away.
and sighting the (island of) Cyprus, and leaving it on left side, did we ourselves sail away to Syria, and did came to Tyre; because there was the ship supposed to unload its cargo.
and after the as we had found the disciples, did we there remain seven days; and they did speak to Paul through the Spirit (the Holy), not to go up to Jerusalem.
and when we had completed the days, did we go out and sail away; and all did us accompany with the women and children till outside the city; and we did kneel on the sea shore and prayer did;
then did we ourselves bid farewell one with the other, and did board on the ship, they however have themselves return home.
and we did finish the sea journey from Tyre, and did arrive to Ptolemais; and giving greetings of peace to the brothers, did we remain with them one day.
and the next morning did we go out, and did come to Caesarea; and did enter in the house of Philip the herald, one of the seven, and stayed with him.
the this one (Philip) did have four daughters virgins, who did prophecies say.
and while we did (there) stay a many days, did come down from the (land) Yehudah a certain prophet, with the name Agav (Agabus).

and coming to us, did he take Paul's belt, has himself bind the feet and the hands, and said: this says the Spirit the Holy: the man, whose belt this is, will the Judaeans in Jerusalem in this way bind, and (him) give over into Goyishe hands into.
and when we did this hear, did we and the local people him begged, that he shall not going up to Jerusalem.
then did Paul answer: what do you (PL), that you (PL) weep and break me the heart? because I am ready not only bound to become, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the L-rd Yehoshua.
and since he has himself not allowed to be persuaded, did we quiet keep silent, so to say: may happen the L-rd's will!
and after the these days did we pack up our things, and did go up to Jerusalem.
and are also accompany with us some of the disciples from Caesarea, bringing along a certain Mnason, from Cyprus, an early on disciple, with whom we have supposed to stay.
and when we are come to Jerusalem, did the brothers us welcome with joy.
and the next day is Paul with us went in to James, and all elders are come there.
and giving greetings of them peace, did he at length report all, that Hashem has done among the nations of the world through his ministry.
and on hearing this, did they praise Hashem; and to him said: you (SG) you see, brother, how many thousands (of) Jews there are, who believe, and all are zealots for the Torah;

and they have they (falsely report) reported about you (SG), that you (SG) teach all Jews, who find self among the nations of the world, self to fall away (from) the (law of) Moses, saying, that they should not circumcise do the children, and themselves not observe do according to the (Jewish) customs.
what then will be? in any case will they (after all) hear, that you (SG) have come.
do therefore this, which we will (to) you say: with us can be found four men, who have a vow upon themselves;

take the these and cleanse you with them, and pay for them, so that they should themselves allow shaving the head; and all will know, that in this, what they have heard about you (SG), there is nothing (any truth). but that you (SG) yourself go also on the way of straight (way of Hashem), and are shomer mitzvot the Torah.

and concerning the Goyishe believers, did we already write a letter, concluding, that they should themselves refrain (to eat) of sacrifices to idols and of blood and of strangled (meat) and of fornication.

Paul did then take the men, did himself ritually purify with them the next day, and did enter in house HaMikdash into, and let know the fulfilment of the days of ritual purification, until it shall brought to be the sacrifice for every one of them.
and when the seven days have self now almost completed, did Judaeans from (Minor) Asia him caught sight of in house HaMikdash, and did stir up the entire crowd, and did place their hands on him,

shouting, men of Israel, help: the this one man is it, who teaches everyone everywhere against the (Jewish) people and the Torah and the this place (holy), even more, he did even lead in Greeks in House HaMikdash into and did desecrate the these place holy.
because they have previously had seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him; and thought, that Paul had him led in into House HaMikdash into.
and the whole city has self moved, and there is become a turmoil of people; and they did seize Paul and him drag out outside the House HaMikdash; and immediately have self the doors shut.
and as they did him want to kill, did come a report to the captain of the cohort, that all Jerusalem is in an uproar.
did he quickly take soldiers and officers, and did run down to them; and seeing the captain and the soldiers, did they stop to beat up Paul.
then did the captain go over, did him arrest, and ordered they should him bind with two chains, and did ask, who he is, and what he has done.
and every one in the crowd did something else shout; and not being able himself to find out for certain, on account of the commotion, did he order, they should him lead away in the garrison into.
and when he is come to the steps, have the soldiers him carried on account of the crush of the crowd;
because the mass of people did follow, shouting: went away with him!
and when Paul was about to brought in to be in the garrison into, did he say to the captain: (question) is it me permit something to say to you (SG)? and he has said: you (SG) know Greek?
(question) you are then not the Egyptian, who did with a certain time back make an insurgency, and led out in the wilderness into the four thousand men of the assassins?
did Paul say: I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of a prominent city; ask I you, allow me to speak to the people.

and when he did it him permit, did Paul himself stand on the steps, and made a sign with the hand to the people; and that it is became a great quietness, did he speak to them on language holy, so to say:
brothers and fathers, hear now out my defense before you (PL)—
and when they did hear, that he speaks to them on language holy, did they themselves even quieter behave; and he did say—

I am a Jew, born in Tarsus in Cilicia, brought up however am I become (here) in the this city, at the feet of (Tanna Rabban) Gamliel, and one has me diligently taught the Torah of our fathers, and a zealot am I was for Hashem, as you (PL) all are up to today's day.
and the this (way of Hashem) way did I persecute to the death, binding and turning over into prison into men and women.

as even the kohen gadol will it me witness say and the whole house of the elders, from whom I did received letter to the brothers, and did go to Damascus to bring also those, who are there were, bound to Jerusalem, so that they should punished to be.
and it is happened, while I was on the way and did me come near to Damascus, around half day did me suddenly shone around a great light from heaven.
and I did fall down on the ground, and did hear a voice say to me: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?
and I did answer: who you are, L-rd? and he did to me say: I am Yehoshua of Natseret, whom you (SG) persecute.
and the (ones), who were with me was, have seen the light, but this voice, which has spoken with me, have they not (with understanding) heard.
and I have said: what shall I do, L-rd? and the L-rd did to me say: stand up, go to Damascus; and there will you (SG) (already) told to be about everything, which is you (SG) appointed been, to do.
since however I was not able to see because of the glory of that light, am I come to Damascus, led by the hand of those, who were with me was.
and a certain Chananyah, a devout man according to the Torah, who has had a good name with all Jews, who did there dwell,
is come to me, and is standing beside me, said: brother Saul, become again seeing! and in the same hour did I look on him.
and he has said: the G-d of our fathers has you chosen, to know his will and to see the Righteous One and to hear a voice from his mouth out.
because you (SG) will be a witness for him to all people of that, which you (SG) have seen and heard.
and now why delay? stand up, let you immersed be in the mikveh, and wash away your sin, calling upon his Name.
and it is happened, while I have me returned to Jerusalem and did prayer done in House HaMikdash, am I fell in into a trance,
and have him seen say to me: hurry yourself, and go out quickly from Jerusalem, because they will (here) not accept your witness say about me.
and I did say: L-rd, they themselves know (after all), that I used to put them in prison and beat up in all the synagogues the (ones), who believe in you (SG);
and while the blood of your witness Stefanos is shed being, was I myself standing nearby agree being (thereto), and guard giving over the clothing of the (ones), who did him kill.
and he did to me say: go; because I will you send far away to the nations of the world.
and they did him listened to until to the this word; and did lift up their voice, saying: away with such people from the earth; because he is not worthy that he lives!
and while they have (so) shouted and thrown down the cloaks (from themselves) and toss dust in the air,

has the captain commanded, he shall brought in to be in the garrison into, and did order, they should him examine with lashes, so that self to find out, on account of what reason they have so shouted against him.

as however they had him outstretched to flog, did Paul say to the officer, who was standing nearby: (question) is (for) you then allowed to flog a man, who is a Roman citizen and who is not condemned?
and as the officer has this heard, has he went to the captain and to him reported, so to say: what go you to do? the this man is after all a Roman!
and the captain is come over and said to him: tell me, you (SG) are (actually) a Roman? has he said: yes.
has the captain answered: for a great price have I me obtained the this citizenship. and Paul did say: I however am born become (a Roman).
and those, who had him should examine, are therefore immediately go away from him; and the captain did self fear, finding out self, that he is a Roman, and that he had him allowed to be bound.

the next morning however, wanting himself to find out for certain, about what he is accused being by the Judaeans, did he him set free from the chains, and ordered, that the chief kohenim should self gather together and the entire Sanhedrin: and did lead down Paul, and him puts before them.
and Paul did himself gazing intently on the Sanhedrin, and said: brothers, I have lived before Hashem with a whole and good conscience until to the present day.
however the kohen gadol Chananyah did order the (ones), who are there with him standing, him to strike on the mouth.
did Paul then to him say: Hashem will you strike, you (SG) white chalked wall; and you (SG) sit me to judge according to the Torah, and order they shall me strike contrary to the Torah?
however the (ones), who were there standing did say: the kohen gadol of Hashem you berate?
did Paul say: brothers, I did not know, that it is the kohen gadol; because it stands written: a ruler to your nation shall you (SG) not curse. (Exodus 22, 27.)

and knowing, that one part is Sadducees and the other part Pharisees, did Paul a shout do in the Sanhedrin: brothers, I am a Pharisee son of Pharisees; about the hope of resurrection of the dead ones am I judged!
and when he had this said, there is become a dispute from the Pharisees with the Sadducees, and the crowd did themselves split.
because the Sadducees say, that there is there is not any resurrection of the dead ones, not any angel, nor any spirit; the Pharisees however are confessing to both.

and there is become a great outcry; and it did stand up some scribes of the side of the Pharisees, and did hold a dispute, thus to say: we find not any whatever evil in the this man; and (what is) if a spirit or an angel did to him speak?

and when the dispute is become (really) great, did the captain, fear having, that Paul shall by them not torn apart become, ordered the soldiery to come down and him a seize to do from their midst, and lead into in the garrison into.
and in the following night did the L-rd stand by him, and said: be strong; because as you (SG) did witness said about me in Jerusalem, so must you also witness say in Rome.
and when it is become day did the Judaeans made a plot, and themselves bound with a solemn oath, and said, that they will not to eat and not drink until they will not kill Paul.
and there are were more than forty, which did make the this oath.
and they did come to the chief kohenim and to the elders, and did say: with a solemn oath have we ourselves bound nothing taste to be, until we will not kill Paul.

therefore let now with the Sanhedrin make known to the captain, that he shall him bring down to you (PL), exactly as you (PL) would wanted with exactitude to examine about him; and before he will self get closer to you (PL), are we ready him to kill.
but Paul's sister's son had heard of the ambush, and is come, and entered in the garrison into, and did this report Paul.
and Paul did call one of the officers, and said: lead the this young man to the captain, because he has him something to tell.
and he did him take and brought him to the captain, and said: the prisoner Paul did me call and asked, I shall bring to you (SG) the this young man, who has something to you (SG) to say.
and the captain did him take by the hand, did him led away on a side, and (him) asked: what is it, that you (SG) you have me to tell?

did he say: the Judaeans have agreed you to ask, that you (SG) you shall tomorrow morning bring down Paul to the Sanhedrin, just as if like they would want something with exactitude to investigate about him.

you (SG) you shall yourself however not permit be persuaded by them, because more than forty (men) of them lie in wait (for ambush) for him, and have themselves solemn sworn, not to eat and not to drink, until they will him not have killed; and are now ready and wait (only) on your consent.
and the captain did send away the young man, enjoining him: you shall any one not tell, that you (SG) you have me this to know done.
and did call two of the officers, and said: prepare to two hundred soldiers, who should go to Caesarea, and seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen, in the third (9 P.M.) hour of the night;
and (he has order) they should prepare beasts, so that mounted (on a horse) Paul and him led away in safety to Felix the governor.
and did write a letter, in this manner:
Claudius Lysias to the eminent governor Felix, peace.
the this man is captive become by the Judaeans, and they did him want to kill; (but) I did come with the soldiery and did him rescue, finding out myself, that he is a Roman.
and wanting to know the reason, for which they had him accused, did I him lead down to their Sanhedrin;
and did find, that he being accused about questions of their Torah, and had not any whatever indictment, that he shall be deserve death or chains.
when however it is me disclosed become, that it will be a plot on the man, have I him immediately sent to you (SG), ordered also the accusers to speak before you (SG) against him.
the soldiers did therefore take Paul, according to as it was them ordered become, and him led away by night to Antipatris.
and the next morning, allowing the horsemen to go with him, did they themselves return to the garrison into;
and they did go in to Caesarea and did hand over the letter to the governor, and also presented Paul before him.
and after reading, did he him ask from which province he is; and as he has heard, that from Cilicia,
did he say: I will you hear, when the accusers your will also (here) come; and did order, they should him guard in Herod's palace.
and five days later did the kohen gadol Chananyah come down with some elders, and a trial lawyer orator, a certain Tertullus; and did appeared (to make charges) before the governor against Paul.

and when he is called become, did Tertullus begin him to accusing, saying: that we enjoy much peace through you (SG), and that a many improvements are done become to the this nation through your oversight,
(this) acknowledge we always and everywhere, o noble Felix, with much thankfulness.
but in order to I shall you not too much detain, beg I you in your gentleness us to hear briefly.
because we have found the this very man as a pest, and an inciter to dissensions among all Jews over the entire inhabited world, a leader of the sect of the Nazerenes;
that he has also made an attempt desecrating to do the House HaMikdash; and we have him arrest and wanted to judge according to our Torah.
but Lysias the captain did come and with force him torn out of our hands,
ordering his accusers to come to you (SG); from whom, after a close examination, you (SG) you will yourself be able to find out, all the these things, about which we accuse him.
and the Judaeans have joined in did, saying, that it is so.
and Paul did answer, after that as the governor did him given a sign to speak. knowing, that you (SG) are already of how many years a judge by the this nation, defend I myself with good courage;
because you (SG) can self find out, that it is not more than twelve days, since I am gone up to Jerusalem, self to worship to Hashem;
and not have they me found holding a debate with anyone or making a dispute with the crowd in the House HaMikdash, not in the synagogues, not in the city,
and they can you (SG) even not prove that, about which they accusing me now.

but the these am I myself before you (SG) confessing, that according to the (way of Hashem) way of, which they call an sect, just so serve I the G-d of our fathers, believing all, what stands written in the Torah and in the prophets;
and have a hope to Hashem, which they themselves wait for, that it will be a resurrection of the dead ones of righteous and unrighteous.
therefore trouble I myself always to have a pure conscience before Hashem and before people.
and after many years am I come to bring alms to my nation, and sacrifices;
with which they have me found, after the as I did myself sanctify in the House HaMikdash, not with any crowd of people and not with any commotion; but there are here some Judaeans from (Minor) Asia,
who should ought appeared before you (SG) and make an accusation, if they have something against me.
or should the these (men) themselves say, what for an injustice they have found in me, when I am standing before Sanhedrin,
except about the this only word, which I did cry out, standing among them: about resurrection of the dead ones am I today judged by you (PL).
Felix however, knowing the (way of Hashem) way precisely, did them defer, and said: when Lysias the captain will come down, will I decide your matter.
and did order the officer him to guard with mildness, and not to hinder anyone from his friends him to serving.
and in some days later did Felix come with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul, and him listened to about the faith (way of Hashem) in the Moshiach Yehoshua.

and while he did speak about righteousness, and victory over inclination (to) evil, and the judgment future to come (Day of Judgment), did Felix himself grow anxious, and answer: now go you (SG) already; and when I will have a convenient time, will I you again permit summon.
at the same time did he also hope, that it would him given to be money from Paul, so that he should him release, on account of that did he also more often let send after him and with him speak.
and when two years did flow by, did Felix received Portius Festus for the successor; and wanting to show the Judaeans a favor, did Felix leave Paul in prison.
and Festus, coming in the province into, did in three days around went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
and the chief kohenim and the most prominent Judaeans did appear before him against Paul, and did him begged,
demanding a favor against him (thatis Paul), that he shall him allow to be brought to Jerusalem; because they had made a plot him to kill on the way.
Festus however did answer, that Paul remains under watch in Caesarea, and himself will he in a short time about to depart there.
therefore should the most powerful among you (PL), did he say, go down (with me), if there is here something an injustice in this man, shall they him accuse.
and after remaining with them no longer than eight or ten days, is he go down to Caesarea; the next morning did he himself sat down on the tribunal seat, and ordered, should bring Paul.
and when he did come, did themselves the Judaeans, who were come down from Jerusalem, stand around him, bringing a many and heavy accusations, which they were not able to prove;
while Paul did himself defend: not against the Jewish Torah, not against the Beis HaMikdash, not against Caesar have I anything sinned.
Festus however, wanting to find favor with the Judaeans, did answering Paul say: (question) you want going up to Jerusalem, and there by me judged to be about the these things?
did Paul say: I stand before Caesar's tribunal seat, where I must judged to be; Judaeans have I not done no any injustice, as even you (SG) know this quite well.

and if I am after all committed a crime, and have done something, for which I am deserve death, avoid I me not to die; if however any thing is not (truth), of which they accusing me, can me no one not give over to them. I appeal to the Caesar.
then did Festus self confer with his advisors, and did answer: to the Caesar you have appealed, to the Caesar will you go!
and after the course of some days, did the king Agrippa with Bernice come to Caesarea and did greet Festus.
and given that they have there spend time a many days, did Festus put before the king Paul's case, saying: Felix did left behind a certain man in chains,
about whom, when I am come to Jerusalem, the Jewish chief kohenim and elders did appeared before me, demanding a verdict against him;

whom I did answer, that it is not the custom with Romans to give over a man (to the death) before the accused has the accusers before himself face to face, and receives an opportunity himself to defend on the accusation.
when therefore they did themselves here come together, did I not make any delay, (but immediately) the next day me sat on the tribunal seat and ordered, should bring the man.
against whom the accusers, standing up themselves, did not bring no any indictment of crimes, as I had suspected was,
but did have certain complaints to him about their own faith, and about a certain Yehoshua, who is died, and who Paul says, that he lives.
and I, being in doubt about the investigation of such questions, did ask, if he wants go to Jerusalem and there judged to be about the these matters.
since however Paul did appeal, to remain in arrest until to the Caesar's decision, have I order, he shall guarded to be, until I will him send to the Caesar.
and Agrippa did say to Festus: I myself would also want hear the man. tomorrow, did he say, will you him hear.

the next morning therefore, when Agrippa is come with Bernice with great fanfare, and did go in in the great hall with the military commanders and most prominent men of the city, did Festus give an order, should bring Paul.

and Festus did say; King Agrippa, and you (PL) all men, who are (here) present with us, you (PL) see the this (man), about whom the whole mass of the Judaeans has me begged in Jerusalem and also here, shouting, that he may longer not live.
I did however understand, that he had nothing done, for which he shall be liable death; but because he himself has appealed to the Caesar, did I decide him to send.

I have however not something specific to write about him to my Master. therefore did I him bring before you (PL), and above all before you (SG), King Agrippa, so that after the investigation shall I have what to write.
because it seems me from not logical, to send a prisoner, and not to present the accusations against him.
and Agrippa did say to Paul: it is you (SG) permitted to speak for yourself. then did Paul stretch out the hand and himself defended:
I value myself fortunate, o King Agrippa, that I must myself today defend before you (SG) about all, which the Judaeans accuse me on;
above all because you (SG) are a knowledgeable of all customs and questions among Jews; therefore beg I you, you (SG) you shall me hear out with patience.
who concerning my manner of life from the youth onwards, which was from the very beginning among my people in Jerusalem, know all Jews,
and know me already for long time, they should only want witness say, that according to the strictest sect of our faith did I live, a Pharisee.
and now stand I judged to be on account of the hope of the promise, which Hashem did make to our fathers,
to whom our twelve tribes, serving Hashem with diligence day and night, hope to obtain. about that hope am I accused by the Judaeans, o King!
why consider it be it with you (PL) for unbelievable, that Hashem wake on the dead?
I myself actually did me think, that I must a many do against the name of Yehoshua of Natseret.
and did it also do in Jerusalem; and much of the holy ones did I lock in prisons, having received power of the chief kohenim; and when they has them killed did I agree to it.
and in all synagogues did I them often punish, and them compelled to blaspheme; and being extremely furious on them, did I them persecute even as far as cities outside the country.
and while I was traveling about that to Damascus with authority and warrant of the chief kohenim,
did I in middle of day see on the way, o King, a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, (which) did me shone around and the (ones), who were traveling with me.
and when we all did fall down on the ground. did I heard a voice, which did to me say in language holy: Saul, Saul why do you persecute me? it is hard for you (SG) to push against the pointed goads.
and I had said: who you are, L-rd? and the L-rd has said: I am Yehoshua, whom you (SG) persecute.

but begin you on, and stand yourself on your feet; because for the this did I myself to you (SG) appear, you to make for a servant and witness of that, which you (SG) have seen of me, and of the things, in which I will myself to you (SG) appear;
I will you save do from that (Judaean) people and from the nations (of the world), to which I send you,

to open up their eyes, that they should themselves return from the darkness to the light, and from the power of the Satan to Hashem, so that they should received forgiveness of sin, and an inheritance among those, who are holy become through (way of Hashem) faith in me.
therefore, o King Agrippa, am I not become disobedient to the vision from heaven;

but first to those in Damascus and in Jerusalem, and over entire land Yehudah, and to the nations of the world have I preached, that they should repentance do and themselves return to Hashem, and do deeds (good), which are worthy of repentance.
for the this have me Judaeans seized in the House HaMikdash, and did attempt me to kill.

therefore since I have received the help, which is from Hashem, stand I until to the today's day, witness saying before small and before great, and tell not any in no way thing except this, which the prophets and Moses (Rebbeinu) did say, that it would happen:
that the Moshiach will suffer, and that He, the first to rise resurrection of the dead ones, will proclaim a light to the (Jewish) people and to the nations (of the world).
and while he had so spoken for his defense, did Festus say with a loud voice: Paul, you (SG) have lost from senses; the great learning leads you to madness.
Paul however did say: I am not crazy, o noble Festus, but I speak words of truth and sobriety.

because about the these things, knows the king, to whom I speak also with boldness; because I am confident, that of the these things is him nothing hidden, because it is not done become in a (secret) corner.
King Agrippa, (question) do you believe the prophets? I know, that you (SG) believe!
and Agrippa (did say) to Paul: it lacking not any many, and you (SG) have me persuaded to become a (way of Hashem) Meshichist!

and Paul (did say): I wish, shall Hashem give, whether with few or with a many, that not only you (SG) yourself, but also all, who hear me today, shall become such, as I am, (but) without the these chains.
and the king is stand up again and the governor and Bernice and the (ones), who are sitting with them;
and while departing, did they speak one with the other, so to say: the this one man has nothing done, for which he shall be liable death or chains.
and Agrippa did say to Festus: the this one man would be able set free to be, if he would not appealed to the Caesar.
and as it is decided been, that we should ourselves sail away to Italy, has they handed over Paul with some other prisoners to an officer, with the name Julius, from the (Augustus) Caesar's cohort.
and after boarding on a ship from Adramyttium, which was about to go to the ports of the (Minor) Asian sea shores, did we sail away, and on our account was Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica.
and the next day did we arrive to Tzidon; and Julius has self behave humanely to Paul, and him permit to go to his friends, so that to come to self (his needs provided for).
and from there did we depart and ourselves sailed passing (the island of) Cyprus, on account of that, which the winds are were against us.
and sailing over the sea beside Cilicia and Pamphylia, did we come to Myra in Lycia.
and there did the officer find an Alexandrian ship, which was sailing to Italy, and did us seat upon on the this one.
and in the course of a many days did we travel slowly and did barely arrive to Cnidus, and because the wind did us not allow, did we travel past (a lee of) the (island of) Crete, opposite Salmone;
and sailing away with effort by the sea shore, did we come to a place, which was called Fair Havens near of the city of Lasea.
and when a many time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous, because of also the Fast (Day of Atonement) is already was past, did Paul them warn,
saying to them: men, I see one, that the voyage will be tied in with danger and much harm, not only for the cargo and the ship, but also for our lives.
the officer however did more believe the captain and the owner of the ship, than Paul's words.

and given that the port was not was spacious, there to spend the winter, did the majority advise from there to leave, perhaps will they be able to arrive to Phoenix—a harbour of Crete, which lies (protected) against the north west and south west winds—and spend the winter.
and while the south wind did gently blow, thinking that they had achieved their goal, did they did hoist the anchor, and did sail past Crete, near by the shore.
but not long afterwards has self picked up against her (the ship) a windstorm, which called the Northeaster; and did a seize done the ship,
and when she has self already more not be able withstand the wind, did we give in and were carried become (by the waves).
and running thus behind a small island, which was called Clauda, is it us barely successful with great effort to hold on the (rescue) boat/skiff;

and when it (skiff) has it hoisted, have they used supports (cables), to undergird the ship; and fearing self, lest will they driven to be on the shallows, did they lower the sail and they is thus driven become.
and because we have hard suffered from the windstorm, has they the next day throw out the cargo;
and the third day has they with their own hands throw out the ship's gear.

and since during of several days not the sun nor the stars have self appeared, and the storm, not any small one, did (on us) press self, is end as long end vanish every hope, that we should saved to be.

and given that they has already long not had eaten, did Paul himself stand in their midst and say: o men, you (PL) did me ought to hear, yourselves not to sail away from Crete, and you (PL) would yourselves have spared the these suffering and the harm/loss.
now however demand I you (PL) on, yourselves to strengthen; because it will any soul of you (PL) not lost to be, except the ship.
because in the this night did by me stand an angel of Hashem, whose I am and whom I serve,
so to say: fear you not, Paul; you (SG) must stand before Caesar; and look, Hashem did you (SG) give as a gift all, who travel with you (SG).
therefore, men, have courage; because I believe Hashem, that it will be exactly the way, as it is me told was.
we must however run aground to be on some sort of an island of.
and when it is come the fourteenth night, and we are driven become over the Adriatic sea, did the sailors notice around half night, that they get closer self to some sort of a land;
did they lower the sink lead and found twenty fathoms (deep); did a little further travel and again lowered the lead, and did find fifteen fathoms (deep).
and fear having, we should not fall on rocky places, did they throw out four anchors from the stern (back) of the ship, and prayer done, that it should (already) to be day.
but as the sailors had sought to flee from the ship, and had already did lower the (rescue) boat under pretext, that they go lower anchors off the bow,
did Paul say to the officer and to the soldiers: if the these will not remain on the ship, can you (PL) not saved to be.
did the soldiers then chopped off the ropes from the boat, and it let fall away.
but until it will not become daytime, did Paul (to) everyone ask, to take something to eat, saying: today is (already) the fourteenth day that you (PL) wait not eating, and did nothing taste did.
therefore beg I you (PL), to take food, because the these has to do with your salvation; because anyone of you (PL) will even one hair from the head not lost become.
and having this said, did he take bread, and thanked Hashem for (to) everyone; and did it break, and began to eat.
and all have self strengthen, and also took food.
and we all in the ship are was two hundred and six and seventy souls.
and after the when they have eaten to the sated, did they light (lighten) made the ship, and threw out the wheat in sea into.
when however it is become day, did they not recognize the land; did however notice a bay with a shore, and decided, if possible to bring up/drive the ship on the shore.
and did chop off the anchors, leaving them in sea, and the same time did they loose up made the cords of the rudders; and did hoist the sail against wind, and themselves a let done to the shore to.
falling however on a sand bank, did they bring up the ship on the ground; and the bow is remain fast, immovable, the stern (back) however has self break by the intensity of the waves.
and the soldiers had in mind to have to kill the prisoners, so that anyone shall not swim away and escape.
but the officer, wanting to save Paul, did them prevent in the plan, and ordered, that those, who can swim, should the first themselves throw in (in sea into) and come to the land;
and the remaining, some on boards, some on something (else) from the ship. and so did it to happen, that all have themselves saved on the dry land upwards.
and after the as we are saved become, did we ourselves then find out, that the island is called Malta.

and the barbarians did us show an extraordinary humaneness; because they did kindle a bonfire and us everyone welcomed on account of the rain, which did set in in one to fall and on account of the chill.
and Paul did gather together a bundle kindling and it did place on the bonfire, and a viper did come out, because of the heat, and has itself hung on his hand.

and when the barbarians did see the creature dangling on his hand, did they say one to the other: the this man is surely a murderer, who, although he has escaped from the sea, allows him yet the justice not to live.
he however did shaking off the creature in fire into, and it has him nothing harmed.

and they have expected, that he will swell up become or suddenly fall down dead; when however they have long waiting, and saw, that it occurs him not any in no way harm, did they change their mind, and said, that he is a g-t.
and near of that place of was land (owner), land who has belong to the chief of the island of, with the name Publius; who did us welcomed and three days friendly hosted us,
and Publius's father is (just happened that) lying sick on a fever and dysentery; to whom Paul is go in and pray, and placing on the hands on him, did he him healed.
and when the these is happened, are also the remaining sick on the island of come, and themselves allowed (to be) healed;
and did us lavish great honors; and when we did departing (to sail away on the ship), have they us supplied everything necessary.
three months later are we sail away in an Alexandrian ship, which had wintered on the island; its figurehead was the Twin Brothers.
and we are come to Syracuse, and are there remain three days.
from there are we tacked away and are come to Rhegium; and one day later has self got up a south wind, and the next day did we come to Puteoli,
where we did find brothers, who did us beg to remain with them seven days, and so are we come to Rome.
and from there did the brothers, on hearing about us, us came out to meet until to the Appii Forum and Three Taverns; seeing them, did Paul give a praise to Hashem and himself strengthened.
and when we did come to Rome, has they Paul permit to dwell (his own quarters) himself with the soldier, who had him guarded.

and it is happened, in three days around has he call together the (ones), who are was the most prominent among the Judaeans; and when they did themselves come together, did he to them say: brothers, although I have nothing done against our people or the customs of our fathers, am I still handed over become as a prisoner from Jerusalem to the Romans in the hands into,
who, after the as they have me examined was, have wanted me release, because it in me not was any death guilt.
but since the Judaeans have self opposed, am I was compel to appeal to the Caesar; not that I would have something which bring charge against my people.
and for the this reason have I you (PL) called, so that you (PL) to see and to you (PL) to speak, because about the hope of Israel am I bound with the this one chain.
and they have to him said: not we have acquired letter from the (land) Yehudah about you (SG), not (nor) is someone of the brothers come, who has reported or said something evil regarding you (SG).
we want however to hear from you (SG), what you (SG) think; because which relates to the this sect, is us known, that everywhere speak they against it.

and after the as they have him appointed a day, are they come to him in guest house into in greater numbers; to whom he did declare, witness saying about the kingdom of Hashem, and proving about Yehoshua from law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until in evening.
and a part have self let convinced from what was said, others however did not believe.

and since they were not in agreement among themselves, are they went away, after the as Paul has after said one word: well did the Spirit the Holy speak through the prophet Isaiah to your (PL) parents, so to say:
go to the this people and say:
because dull/fat become is the heart of the this people,
therefore be know, that the this salvation of Hashem is being sent to the nations of the world; and they will (it) hear.
(and when he did this say, are the Judaeans gone away, holding a great dispute among themselves.)
and he is remain whole two years in his own rented house, and received all, who are come in to him,
did proclaim the kingdom of Hashem and taught of the L-rd Yehoshua the Moshiach all openly, by anyone not prevented.
Paul, a slave of Yehoshua the Moshiach, called to be a Shliach, set apart for the News Good of Hashem,
which he had from before promised through his prophets in the Scriptures the Holy,
about His Son, who is born become of the seed (of) David according to flesh,
decisively shown as the Son of the Most High with power, according to the Spirit of holiness through the resurrection from the dead—Yehoshua the Messiah our L-rd,
through whom we have received grace and the Shlichus to the obedience of the faith among all peoples for the sake of His Name,
among whom also you (PL) are called of Yehoshua the Moshiach;
to all, who are in Rome, beloved of Hashem, called (to be) holy ones: grace to you (PL) and peace from Hashem our Father and from the L-rd Yehoshua the Moshiach.
before all give I up a praise to my G-d through Yehoshua the Moshiach for you (PL) all, since about your (way of Hashem) faith is spoken of in the whole world.
for Hashem, whom I serve in my spirit in the News Good of His Son, is my witness as I remember you (PL) without stopping
in my prayers, asking always, that it may me already succeed, if wills (it) Hashem, to you (PL) to come.
for my desire is you (PL) to see, so that you (PL) to give over something a spiritual gift to your strengthening;
this means, I shall comforted to be in you (PL) through the mutual (way of Hashem) faith, yours and mine.

and I want not, brothers, you (PL) shall be uninformed, that often have I already wanted come to you (PL) (and am until now prevented become), so that I shall have fruit also among you (PL), as among the other nations.
I am a master of debt to Greeks and to barbarians, to wise ones and to fools.
so then am I ready according to my opportunities to proclaim the News Good also to you (PL) in Rome.
for I ashamed self not with the (way of Hashem) News Good of the Moshiach, because it is Hashem's power to salvation for every one of the believers, the Jew before all and also the Greek.
because in it (way of Hashem) is righteousness of Hashem revealed become from faith to faith, as it stands written: the tsaddik will through his faith live. (Habakuk 2, 4.)
because Hashem's anger reveals itself from heaven upon every wickedness and iniquity of men, who suppress the truth in unrighteousness;
because the knowledge of Hashem is known made to them, because Hashem has it to them reveal did.
because the invisible things His, since the world's creation, become clear through created things, (namely) His eternal power and deity, so that they shall be without an excuse:
on account of that, that knowing Hashem, have they him not glorified as Hashem or (him) thanked, but have themselves to fool made with their mind and their senseless heart is darkened become.
thinking, that they are wise, did they themselves become fools,
and exchanged the glory of the immortal G-d with the likeness of the form of a mortal man and of birds and of four footed and creeping creatures.
therefore did them Hashem handed over in the lusts of their hearts, to filthiness, to shame their bodies among self alone;
who did exchange the (way of Hashem) truth of G-d with a lie and honored and served the created instead the Creator, the Holy One blessed (be) He forever. Amen.
on account of the things has Hashem them given over to shameful lusts; because their women have exchanged the natural use with an unnatural;

and in this way also the men, deserting the natural use of the woman, did themselves in their desiring get heated up one with the other, men with men doing debased things, and did receive in themselves alone the appropriate reward from their misleadings.
and since they have not wanted to have Hashem in their knowledge, did Hashem them handed over to a corrupt understanding, to do that, which one does not;
they are filled become with every nastiness, evil doing, fornication, lascivious lusts greed, malice, full with envy, murder, strife, deceit/treachery, craftiness, slander,
language evil, haters of Hashem, impertinent faces, arrogant, braggert, inventive of evil, disobedient to parents,
without understanding, covenant-breakers, without natural feelings, unmerciful;
who, although knowing of Hashem's judgment, that the (ones), who do the these things, are liable death, have they not only the these things done, but are even applaud with those, who do them.

therefore you are, o man, who you (SG) you shall not be, who judges, without an excuse; for with what you (SG) judge the other (one), (you) condemn you yourself, because you (SG), which judge, you do the these things;
and we know that Hashem's judgment is according to the truth on the (ones), who do the these things.
do you think then, o man, who judges the (ones), who do the these things and you do they themselves, that you (SG) will evade Hashem's judgment?
or are you degrading the riches of His goodness, patience and forbearance, not knowing, that the goodness of Hashem should you lead to the repentance do?
you (SG) however, according to your hardness and your not repentant heart, store up (for) you (sg) one wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of Hashem's rightful judgment,
who will each one repay according to his works: (Proverbs 24, 2.)
to the (ones), who seek with patience through deeds good—glory, honor and immortality, eternal life;
but to the rebellious and who are disobedient to the truth but are obedient to wickedness—wrath and fury;
suffering and anguish upon every human soul, who does evil, before all the Jewish person and also the Greek (non-Jew).
but glory and honor and peace to everyone, who does good, before all the Jew and also the Greek (non-Jew);
because Hashem does not any partiality of faces. (Deuteronomy 10, 17.)
because all, who have sinned without a Torah, will also without a Torah lost become; and all, who have sinned under the Torah, will judged to be by the Torah;
because not the (ones), who hear the Torah, are right with Hashem, but those, who do (what) the Torah (says), will justify become;
because when the nations of the world, not having the Torah, do by their nature according to (how) the Torah (writes about), they, though not having any Torah, are a law for themselves alone.
they to show, that doing (what stands in) the Torah is written on their hearts, when their conscience said witness and their thoughts either accusing themselves or justifying self mutually;
in the Day when Hashem will judge the secret things of men, according to my News Good through the Moshiach Yehoshua.
but if you (SG) call yourself a Jew and rely yourself on the Torah and boast you with Hashem,
and know His will and, know to differentiate between good and evil, being learned in the Torah,
and are convinced, that you (SG) alone are a guide of the blind—a light for the (ones), who are in the darkness,
an educator for the senseless, a teacher of young children, having the form of knowledge and of truth in the Torah;
therefore you (SG), who teach an other, why teach not you yourself? you (SG) preach, should not steal, and you yourself steal!
you (SG), who say, should not commit adultery, you commit adultery! you (SG) desecrate the idols, (yet) rob the heathen temple?
you (SG), who boast yourself about the Torah, dishonor you (SG) Hashem by break be the Torah!
because Hashem's Name is by you (PL) blasphemed among the nations, just as it stands written. (Yeshayah 52, 5)
because the circumcise do has real a worth, if you (SG) do what the Torah says; but if you (SG) are violating the Torah is your circumcision become an uncircumcision.
therefore, when the not circumcised will observe the laws of the Torah, (question) will him then not his uncircumcision reckoned to be for circumcision?
and will the by nature not circumcised, who does fulfill the Torah, you not condemn, who has the letter and the circumcision and does transgress the Torah?
because not that (one) is a Jew, who is (a Jew) outwardly, circumcision is also not that, which is only outwardly in the body;
but a Jew is the one, who is inwardly such, and circumcision is in the heart according to Spirit, not according to the letter, whose praise is not from men, but from Hashem.
therefore, what for a advantage has the Jew, or what is the benefit of the circumcision?
a many in every case—before all actually because to them (the Jews) is entrusted become that which Hashem has spoken.
and if a part did not believe, what make (does) it then out? (question) makes then their unbelief negate the faithfulness of Hashem?

mercy and peace! let Himself Hashem turn out as truthful and every man a liar, as it stands written: so that you (SG) you shall be right in your words and prevail when you (SG) will be judged. (Psalms 51, 5.)
if however our wickedness shows off the righteousness of Hashem, what shall we say? that Hashem is wrong, bringing wrath? I speak as a man.
mercy and peace! because if so, how would Hashem be able to judge the world?
if however through my lie did itself the truth of Hashem abound to His glory, why should I still judged to be as a sinner?
and why should we not actually—as those, who insult us by asserting, that we say—do the evil, so that the good should come? their judgment is right.
therefore what? (question) have we then some a advantage? never way not! because we have already previously shown, that both the Jewish person and also the Greek are all under the sin;
so as it stands written: there is not there any tsaddik, even one not;
it is not there any understander, it is not there any one, who seeks Hashem;
all have been devious, they are together useless become; it is not there anyone, who does good, no, not one. (Psalms 14, 2-4.)
